sentences.text: The meeting reviewed the conceptual design for a universal TV control, addressing new project requirements such as excluding teletext functionality and incorporating the company's corporate image.
The group discussed various design options including flip-top mechanisms, rechargeable batteries, and ergonomic shapes to address user frustrations with current remote controls.
Presentations covered industrial design concepts, component availability, and market research findings regarding user preferences for aesthetics and usability.
Participant A noted that the previous meeting's plan to use teletext was no longer viable as consumers consider it outdated, and the control is now restricted to TV and video only.
Participant B mentioned that the company's corporate image needs to be incorporated into the design, specifically wanting it to look fashionable and trendy.

Participant D presented an industrial design concept featuring a flip-open mechanism where main functions are on the top and complex programming features are in the middle, noting that most current controls use infrared and are powered by bulky triple-A batteries.
Participant C suggested a flip-top design to simplify interaction, arguing that users typically only use 30-40% of buttons and that a trendy design could appeal to a wide audience.
Participant B presented market research findings indicating that 75% of users find current remotes ugly, 80% would pay more for a fancy look, and 50% are frustrated by losing their remotes.
Participant B reported that 50% of users only use 10% of the buttons on their remotes, leading to potential cost savings by reducing the number of functions.
Participant B highlighted that 34% of users take too much time to learn to use their remotes, and over a quarter cited repetitive strain injury (RSI) as a frustration.
Participant D discussed battery options, noting that rechargeable options were not available at the time, and compared dynamo, solar, and kinetic charging methods.
Participant D explained that kinetic charging, used in wristwatches, relies on movement to charge a small cell, though the duration of battery life was uncertain.
Participant D described the internal circuit board design, noting that printed circuit boards can be printed in varying sizes to fit different button layouts.
The group decided to exclude teletext functionality and limit the control to TV and video use only.
The group decided on a flip design for the remote control.
The group decided to incorporate the company's corporate image into the product design.
The group decided to look into a rechargeable battery option with a docking station.
The group decided to consider a clamshell or shell-like shape for the remote to differentiate it from standard rectangular designs.
